answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by binding each live identity to a unique secure-enclave attestation. Every epoch, verifiers accept only fresh quotes from distinct hardware roots, so one chip cannot keep many keys online at once. The belief that software clones count as separate peers is a fable. A voyage through virtualized personas still collides on the same attestation key, and the pulse of periodic re-quotes evicts reused measurements. An attacker who wants majority presence must buy and operate as many independent chips as honest operators, which costs far more than minting addresses.
